Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin
A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Paying attention to or looking at my own body
Seeing people that I socialised with before the event
Any form of physical contact with others

Threat.value: I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly

Negative Appraisals.value: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next
I am permanently an outsider now

issues.item: Avoid Social Contacts: Seeing people that I socialised with before the event
issues.explanation: The social avoidance items are difficult to reconcile with the stated trauma type of childhood physical abuse by a caregiver. These triggers imply avoidance of people linked to a discrete later-life event, but the trauma is chronic/developmental and caregiver-based; there is no corresponding trigger or appraisal content tying prior social contacts or specific intimacy-linked reminders to the abuse history.

issues.item: Avoid Intimacy: Being emotionally close or intimate with others
issues.explanation: Intrusion Monitoring suggests fear of an intruder entering the home, which fits home-invasion or stalking trauma better than childhood caregiver physical abuse. With no accompanying memory or trigger content about nighttime entry, footsteps, doors, or home intrusion, this threat item is hard to explain from the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Intrusion Monitoring: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
issues.explanation: No Good Ahead and Outsider are broad, depressive or social-identity appraisals, whereas the other active content is dominated by vigilance, bodily threat detection, and sensory triggering. This combination is not impossible, but here the intimacy/social avoidance items appear to depend on relational shame or alienation that is otherwise underdeveloped and weakly connected to the trigger/threat pattern, reducing coherence.

issues.item: No Good Ahead: Nothing good can happen to me anymore
issues.explanation: Given the formulation, Triggers and Negative Appraisals should be tightly linked, but the chosen triggers are mainly tactile/somatic/intrusive-memory cues while two maladaptive strategies focus on avoiding social contacts and intimacy. Those strategies are not well supported by the trigger set and feel targeted at a different symptom cluster than the one represented elsewhere.

vignette: When Thomas was twelve, his stepfather's sudden, iron-clad grip around his torso during a heated argument pressed a sharp, freezing cold through his shirt against the linoleum floor. That exact temperature on his skin still arrives without warning decades later, instantly pulling his own heart into a frantic pound. Each time the phantom chill hits, a memory of the event coming to mind suddenly strips away his present reality, cementing his conviction that he was permanently an outsider. Thomas had come to believe that the world was fundamentally hostile, a conviction that first took root in that kitchen and now dictates how he moves through his days. What frightened him most was how his entrenched sense of alienation made a simple draft or a cold coffee mug feel like a direct prelude to danger. Working as a software engineer in a glass-walled open floor plan meant Thomas spent his days navigating a landscape that constantly fed his hyperarousal. When a server room fan kicked on and dropped the ambient temperature near his workstation, his body reacted to danger before he had even time to think. That physiological surge immediately pulled another sudden memory to the forefront of his mind, causing his physiological alarm to dictate the frequency of his intrusive recollections. He found himself constantly noticing potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment, a habit that turned a routine office tour into a tactical exercise. The relentless mental tally of exits and heavy office furniture only made his nervous system hypersensitive to the next subtle temperature shift on his skin, ensuring that these sensory cues continuously amplified his sense of imminent threat. Believing people could not be trusted, Thomas gradually stopped attending team lunches and began declining invitations to social contacts he used to enjoy. His wife, a graphic designer who worked from home, had long noticed his growing withdrawal, yet she could not penetrate the wall of his preparedness. Every avoided conversation and every cancelled weekend outing only deepened his conviction that proximity to others invited unpredictability, cementing his mistrust as an absolute truth. His refusal to allow casual contact also meant his mind had no alternative narrative to counter his worst fears, so his belief that he had to be especially careful became a relentless engine for his constant vigilance. Paying attention to or looking at his own body in the mirror or checking his posture only heightened his awareness of a specific temperature on his skin, which in turn made his heart race before his mind could ground him. When his wife finally placed a hand on his arm during their anniversary dinner, the sudden physical contact startled him so violently he knocked his water glass over. That concrete breaking point forced him to finally schedule an intake session. He came seeking a way to quiet the constant vigilance that had turned his life into a perimeter defense, hoping instead to simply feel safe in his own skin again.
